images.caption: Salmon Ruins is an unusual monument because it comprises not only ancient Pueblo ruins, outlying from the Chaco canyon settlement in the 11th century, but also a family ranch of the American Southwest homesteaded about 1890 by the Salmons. The photo shows the ranch bunkhouse, which is situated near the stone-walled ruins, of which about two-thirds have been excavated. They lie in the San Juan River valley of New Mexico. Salmon Ruins is on the New Mexico Register of Cultural Properties.
